problem:
The projection of the intersection between the hyperbolic paraboloid $\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=z+2$ and the plane 
$y=3$  onto the $xz$-plane is a parabola. What is the vertex of this parabola?
worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the paraboloid and the plane $y=3$, we substitute $y=3$ into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =z+2 \\ \frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{3}^{2}}{9} & =z+2 \\ \frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4}-1 & =z+2 \\ z+3 & =\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4} \\ z & =\frac{1}{4}(x+1)^{2}-3\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of a parabola in the $xz$-plane that has its vertex at $(-1,-3).$
